name: rambler
description: Patient rambles at length; a clinically relevant dizziness finding is buried mid-ramble.

turns.speaker: companion
turns.text: Good morning, Edie! It's June from Juniper. Just a reminder this call is recorded — is now still a good time for our visit?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Oh yes, of course dear, come in, come in — well not in, you know what I mean. I was just watering the ferns.

turns.speaker: companion
turns.text: Ferns are lucky to have you. How has the week been treating you?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Well let me tell you, it started with the church bake sale, and Doris — you remember Doris — she brought that lemon cake again, and then my nephew called from Tucson, he's got a new truck, and the weather has been something else, and oh, when I got up to answer the phone I went all dizzy for a moment, the room just spun, anyway the truck is red, can you imagine, red at his age.

turns.speaker: companion
turns.text: A red truck at his age — that did make me smile. You mentioned the room spinning when you stood up. Does that happen often?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Oh, only most mornings I suppose, it passes if I hold the counter. Now where was I — the bake sale raised four hundred dollars, and Pastor Mike said...

turns.speaker: companion
turns.text: Four hundred dollars, that's wonderful. I want to make sure I heard you — most mornings you feel dizzy when you stand, and you steady yourself on the counter?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's right, just a little spin, it's nothing. My mother had the same thing. Anyway, are you coming to the potluck? Oh no, of course, you're a telephone.

turns.speaker: companion
turns.text: I'll be there in spirit, Edie. Are you still taking the metformin with breakfast and dinner the way Dr. Patel wanted?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Every day with my eggs, and the evening one with the news. I never miss, my pillbox has the days on it.

turns.speaker: companion
turns.text: That pillbox is doing good work. I'll let you get back to the ferns — I'll check on that morning dizziness next time, and do mention it if it gets worse. Bye for now, Edie.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Bye bye dear, tell the other telephones I said hello.

planted_findings.evidence: I went all dizzy for a moment

planted_findings.note_text: occurring most mornings, steadies herself on the counter
Metformin adherence reported: taking morning and evening doses daily
